answer:
For $p(x_i)=\sum_k\pi_k\mathcal N(x_i;\mu_k,\sigma_k^2)$, the E-step computes responsibilities $r_{ik}=\pi_k\mathcal N(x_i;\mu_k,\sigma_k^2)/\sum_j\pi_j\mathcal N(x_i;\mu_j,\sigma_j^2)$. With $N_k=\sum_i r_{ik}$, the M-step sets $\pi_k=N_k/N$, $\mu_k=\sum_i r_{ik}x_i/N_k$, and $\sigma_k^2=\sum_i r_{ik}(x_i-\mu_k)^2/N_k$. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book1.html) [2](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

Use the newly updated mean in the variance step and stable log probabilities for responsibilities. Exact EM does not decrease likelihood, but may converge to a local optimum and can encounter a singular component collapsing onto one observation. Use multiple initializations, covariance floors or priors, and a defined policy for tiny/empty components. Stop using likelihood improvement plus parameter diagnostics, not a fixed iteration count alone.
